editorial: This report contains trends that have emerged for the first time today, without repeating records included in normal reports from the last 30 days.

items.title: bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view
items.summary: Gods-eye-view is a spatial intelligence tool that visualizes real-time satellite data on a photorealistic 3D globe in the browser. Developed with JavaScript, this open-source project allows users to track global activity live.

items.title: abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus
items.summary: GitNexus is a code analysis tool that runs in the browser and transforms code repositories into an interactive knowledge graph. Thanks to its serverless structure, it allows you to visualize codebases on GitHub, GitLab, or local files using the Graph RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) method.

items.title: abi/screenshot-to-code
items.summary: Screenshot-to-code is a software tool that converts uploaded screenshots into clean code structures (HTML, Tailwind, React, Vue). It aims to accelerate the development process by turning visual designs directly into working code blocks.

items.title: NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra
items.summary: Ghidra, developed by the National Security Agency (NSA), is a comprehensive analysis tool used for software reverse engineering processes. This Java-based platform provides researchers with a detailed examination environment for inspecting binary files and analyzing code.

items.title: tashfeenahmed/freellmapi
items.summary: FreeLLMAPI is a developer tool that consolidates 34 different free large language model (LLM) providers and 635 endpoints into a single OpenAI-compatible interface. With smart routing and automatic error handling features, it offers the opportunity to use numerous free models from a central point in personal projects.

items.title: Saving 100 terabytes of memory by optimizing 1.1.1.1's DNS cache
items.summary: Cloudflare has managed to reduce memory usage by 100 terabytes thanks to new data structures it developed for its Domain Name System (DNS) cache. This optimization increases the overall performance of the system while lowering server costs for Cloudflare, the network infrastructure that manages internet traffic.

items.title: Microduck
items.summary: Microduck, developed by Pollen Robotics, is a compact control board designed for open-source robotic platforms. Thanks to its modular structure, it aims to simplify hardware integration and motion control in robotic projects.

items.title: Small Models Have Arrived
items.summary: Small language models with low parameters can operate on hardware-constrained devices by offering high performance with less processing power. Compared to large AI systems (LLMs), these models provide faster response times and the possibility of low-cost local installation.

items.title: 507 Mechanical Movements
items.summary: Published in 1868, 507 Mechanical Movements is a technical reference source that visualizes basic machine mechanisms and movement principles. Shedding light on the history of engineering, this digital archive explains the mechanical movements that form the basis of complex systems with simple drawings.

items.title: unsloth/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF
items.summary: Optimized by Unsloth, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next is a multimodal artificial intelligence model that processes visual and text data to produce text output. Offered in GGUF format, this model allows for fast inference on local devices by using hardware resources efficiently.

items.title: EditaLive! Unified Character Video Editing for Live Streaming
items.summary: EditaLive is a new framework that makes human-centric video editing processes real-time in live broadcasts. It maintains facial expression consistency, eliminates the need for offline processing, and makes character editing operations suitable for instant interaction.

items.title: PILOT in the Loop: Live Self-Improvement for Long-Horizon Agents
items.summary: PILOT in the Loop is a method that allows artificial intelligence agents conducting long-term tasks to learn from their own experiences while the process is ongoing. This approach enables agents to use the data they obtain to improve the workflow in real-time and enhance their future performance.

items.title: Agentic Game Development as a Verifiable Trajectory Data Engine for Scaling World Models
items.summary: Instead of traditional video scanning methods used to train world models, game development processes that produce verifiable reward signals, such as those offered by code-based agents, are proposed. This approach aims to make the reinforcement learning processes of large language models more efficient by using the feedback mechanisms provided by executable code.

items.title: Procedura: Agentic 3D Modeling with Procedural Control
items.summary: Procedura is an artificial intelligence framework that creates parametric and editable three-dimensional models from a single image by using the coding ability of large language models. Unlike traditional methods, this system defines objects as code blocks that can be broken down and modified.

items.title: Thinking on Shots: Consistent Multi-Shot Video Editing with Agentic Reasoning
items.summary: The Thinking on Shots method uses agentic reasoning processes to resolve inconsistencies experienced in editing long videos. This approach prevents visual discontinuities and editing errors that occur when breaking videos into segments, offering the possibility of long-term video editing with multiple prompts.

items.title: EasyEffects should be part of every Linux distribution to improve laptop speaker sound quality
items.summary: EasyEffects is an audio effects tool that processes audio signals and improves speaker quality on Linux systems. It is suggested that this software be included by default in all Linux distributions to improve audio performance on laptops.

items.title: OpenOffice does not print on Tuesdays (2009)
items.summary: This 2009 technical legend, which claimed that OpenOffice software did not print on Tuesdays, shows how software bugs can turn into urban legends. Technical analyses reveal that the situation was actually caused by an incompatibility with the printer driver, not a calendar bug.
